title: Applied NLP Engineering
tagline: From tokens to fine-tuned language models: build, evaluate and adapt practical NLP systems for English and Arabic text.
audience: Python-proficient developers and data scientists with basic ML. No prior transformer experience needed.
prerequisites: Google Colab (GPU) or local with uv. Run 00_setup_check before Day 1; see labs/README.md.

outcomes.text: Explain and implement tokenization, embeddings and transformer inference
Build semantic search and text classification systems
Develop structured-output and retrieval-grounded LLM applications
Choose between discriminative decision models and generative LLMs
Fine-tune transformers with supervised and parameter-efficient methods
Evaluate, compare and demonstrate practical NLP solutions

case_study.name: Intelligent Support Ticket Processing
case_study.summary: Given an English or Arabic customer message, identify its intent, find similar historical cases, assign a category and priority, and draft a grounded recommended reply. Every lab adds a component to this system.

sessions.title: Tokenization
outcomes: Explain the tokenization pipeline and subword algorithms (BPE, WordPiece)
Inspect token IDs, special tokens, attention masks and context limits
Measure how tokenizers treat Arabic vs. English, and why it costs money

lab.title: Inspect English and Arabic tokenization
lab.summary: You will compare five tokenizers on our support tickets and quantify the "Arabic token tax".

steps.text: Tokenize a ticket, map IDs ↔ tokens, decode back
Inspect special tokens, padding, attention masks
Compute fertility for EN vs. AR across 5 tokenizers
Write an Arabic normalizer; measure its effect
Find the token-length percentile for max_length

lab.stretch: Train a tiny BPE tokenizer on the tickets

sessions.title: Embeddings
outcomes: Explain dense vectors, cosine similarity and pooling
Choose an embedding model for a multilingual use case
Build and evaluate a semantic search over historical tickets

lab.title: Build semantic search over historical tickets
lab.summary: Embed thousands of tickets, search in English and Arabic, and put a number on retrieval quality.

steps.text: Embed sentences; compute a similarity matrix and a heatmap
Compare mean pooling by hand with the library output
Index historical tickets with NumPy, then FAISS
Evaluate Hit@5 and MRR on test tickets (same-intent relevance)
Cross-lingual: Arabic queries → English history

lab.stretch: Compare two embedding models, or plot a 2-D UMAP of intents

sessions.title: Transformers
outcomes: Explain self-attention, multi-head attention and positional information
Distinguish encoder, decoder and encoder–decoder models and what each is for
Load any model from the Hugging Face Hub and inspect its outputs

lab.title: Open the black box
lab.summary: Look at hidden states and attention, implement attention in NumPy, and watch context change a word's vector.

steps.text: Implement scaled dot-product attention in 10 lines of NumPy
Inspect hidden-state and attention shapes for a ticket
Plot an attention heatmap for chosen layer/head
Contextual embeddings: "charge" in two contexts
Fill-mask in English and Arabic with XLM-R

lab.stretch: Causal mask: compare encoder vs. decoder attention patterns

sessions.title: Decision models
sessions.summary: Decision models: when the answer is a label
outcomes: Build zero-shot and embedding-based classifiers for ticket intent
Evaluate with per-class precision/recall/F1 and confusion matrices
Use thresholds to abstain and route uncertain cases to humans

lab.title: Ticket classification + Day 1 integration
lab.summary: Climb the ladder (TF-IDF → zero-shot → embeddings + LR), evaluate properly, add abstention, and combine it with this morning's search.

steps.text: TF-IDF + logistic regression baseline
Zero-shot NLI on categories; try two label wordings
Embeddings + logistic regression on intents
Report, confusion matrix, EN vs. AR slice
Coverage–accuracy curve; choose τ on validation
Integrate: process_ticket() = classify + top-3 similar

lab.stretch: kNN-vote classifier from the search index; compare errors

sessions.title: Generative LLMs
sessions.summary: Generative LLMs: one token at a time
outcomes: Explain next-token prediction, causal attention and the KV cache
Use chat templates correctly with instruction-tuned models
Choose decoding settings (greedy, temperature, top-p) for a task

lab.title: Run and probe a small instruct model
lab.summary: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on GPU (0.5B on CPU), or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint you set in .env.

steps.text: Render the chat template; count prompt tokens
Inspect the top-10 next-token probabilities
Write your own greedy loop with model() calls
Compare greedy vs. T=0.7 vs. T=1.5 on a reply draft (×3 runs)
Measure prefill vs. decode time; tokens per second

lab.stretch: Ask in Arabic and English; compare quality and token counts

sessions.title: Structured outputs
outcomes: Write production prompts: role, task, constraints, format, examples
Get schema-valid JSON reliably: validation, retries, constrained decoding
Defend against prompt injection hidden inside customer messages

lab.title: Triage tickets into validated JSON
lab.summary: Build analyze(ticket) → TicketAnalysis, then measure validity and accuracy across prompt variants.

steps.text: Write the schema; zero-shot prompt; parse 20 tickets
Add validation + retry; log the validity rate
Static 4-shot vs. dynamic 4-shot (retrieved examples)
Regex for order IDs + LLM for the rest; merge
Run 5 injection attacks; harden the prompt

lab.stretch: Constrained decoding with a custom LogitsProcessor

sessions.title: RAG
outcomes: Build a RAG pipeline: chunk, embed, retrieve, rerank, generate with citations
Improve retrieval with hybrid search and cross-encoder reranking
Evaluate retrieval and groundedness separately

lab.title: Minimal RAG over the help center and past tickets
lab.summary: No framework: about 100 lines you fully understand. Frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack) wrap these same steps.

steps.text: Chunk KB articles by heading; attach metadata
Dense + BM25 retrieval; fuse with RRF
Evaluate Hit@3 on the provided question set
Rerank with a cross-encoder; re-evaluate
Grounded, cited JSON reply; validate citations
Ask an unanswerable question: does it abstain?

lab.stretch: Arabic tickets against the English KB: with and without query translation

sessions.title: Model selection
outcomes: Compare encoder classifiers and LLMs on accuracy, latency and cost
Evaluate generative outputs: validity, faithfulness, LLM-as-judge
Assemble the end-to-end ticket assistant with a cascade design

lab.title: Benchmark, decide, integrate
lab.summary: Put numbers on "encoder vs. LLM", then build the cascade and the full pipeline with error analysis.

steps.text: Same 200 test tickets: encoder vs. LLM zero-shot vs. LLM few-shot
Macro-F1, p50/p95 latency, estimated cost per 1k
Cascade: choose τ; report accuracy vs. % sent to LLM
Wire assist(ticket) end to end; run on 10 EN + 10 AR
Error analysis: label 10 failures by stage

lab.stretch: LLM-as-judge for faithfulness; compare with your own labels

sessions.title: Fine-tuning fundamentals
outcomes: Place fine-tuning on the spectrum of adaptation techniques
Decide when fine-tuning is worth it, and when RAG or prompting is better
Build leak-free train/validation/test splits and a tokenized dataset

lab.title: Prepare a leak-free ticket dataset
lab.summary: The output of this lab (a saved DatasetDict + label maps) feeds Labs 3.2 and 3.4.

steps.text: Explore label distribution and text lengths
Near-duplicate check between train and test with embeddings
Build a realistic low-resource train set (≤ 80 per intent)
Label maps, DatasetDict, tokenization, save to disk
Start the model download for Lab 3.2 / 3.3 in the background

lab.stretch: Generate 100 synthetic Arabic training tickets with the LLM; spot-check 10

sessions.title: Fine-tune an encoder
outcomes: Explain classification heads, logits, softmax and cross-entropy
Fine-tune a multilingual encoder with the Hugging Face Trainer
Read learning curves; prevent overfitting; pick the best checkpoint

lab.title: Fine-tune a ticket intent classifier
lab.summary: About 5 minutes of training on a Colab T4. Start training first, then read the code while it runs.

steps.text: Load the saved dataset; build model with label maps
Train with Trainer + early stopping
Plot train/val loss and macro-F1 per epoch
Test once: English and Arabic; compare to Day 1 embeddings + LR
Save model + tokenizer + label maps; reload; predict

lab.stretch: Data-size ablation: 10 / 25 / 80 per class; plot F1 vs. data

sessions.title: LLM adaptation
outcomes: Explain why full LLM fine-tuning is expensive and how LoRA/QLoRA fix it
Prepare chat-formatted SFT data with loss masking
Run a LoRA fine-tune and measure before vs. after

lab.title: LoRA-tune a small instruct model for ticket triage
lab.summary: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct + LoRA on ~1,500 examples. Trains in about 8–10 min on a T4. Fallback: an instructor-trained adapter.
lab.stretch: Merge the adapter; compare r = 4 vs. r = 32

sessions.title: Evaluate & deploy
outcomes: Compare every model from the bootcamp on one honest leaderboard
Do structured error analysis and behavioural tests
Package a reproducible model and serve it behind a demo app

lab.title: Leaderboard, error analysis, demo
lab.summary: This notebook is also your capstone template for evaluation and serving.

steps.text: Load saved predictions; build the leaderboard with bootstrap CIs
Confusion pairs + tag 10 errors by cause
Run the behavioural test suite
Batch vs. single latency; CPU int8 quantization
Launch the Gradio demo of the full assistant

lab.stretch: Wrap assist() in a FastAPI endpoint

capstone.summary: Teams of 2–3 build an applied NLP solution, choosing one of: Intelligent Support Ticket Assistant: classify, retrieve similar cases, draft grounded replies; Arabic Document Intelligence: extract and categorize; answer questions with evidence; Voice of Customer Analyzer: classify feedback, cluster issues, summarize insights.
capstone.submission: Submit a repository with working code, README, evaluation results and sample inputs/outputs. Template: labs/capstone/.
